content.text: {"comps":[{"label":"C1","good":false,"reason":"Primarily aircraft parts and MRO for airlines and cargo operators; defense shelters are a minor side line, not Parsons' engineering or cyber business."},{"label":"C2","good":false,"reason":"Telecom and media billing, customer management and operations software sold to communications operators, not government defense or infrastructure engineering."},{"label":"C3","good":true,"reason":"Government engineering, technical and mission operations services for defense, intelligence and federal agencies, closely matching Parsons' contract-based model."},{"label":"C4","good":false,"reason":"Manufactures meters, filters, test equipment and aerospace components sold to utilities and OEMs, rather than providing engineering services to government."},{"label":"C5","good":false,"reason":"Sells network security hardware and subscriptions to enterprises and channel partners, a product business unlike Parsons' government-contracted engineering and cyber services."},{"label":"C6","good":true,"reason":"Engineering, consulting and program management for defense, government and transportation clients through contract-based services, closely matching Parsons' model."},{"label":"C7","good":false,"reason":"Construction and maintenance contractor for telecom, energy and pipeline owners, with commercial customers and little government or defense work."},{"label":"C8","good":true,"reason":"Engineering and consulting services sold mainly to government agencies for water and infrastructure, sharing Parsons' government-client service model."}]}
